title: Insertion tabs: Even-key census
topics: Recursion, sorting, binary search and bits
summary: The input contains two rows: a sorted drawer and query values. For each query, produce the first index whose drawer value is at least that query; use the drawer's length if no such index exists. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values.
descriptionMd:
The archive needs insertion tabs for new labels without disturbing an existing sorted drawer. Sol separates readings for the office's even-numbered keys. A zero reading belongs in that count, just like any other even number.

The input contains two rows: a sorted drawer and query values. For each query, produce the first index whose drawer value is at least that query; use the drawer's length if no such index exists.

Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values.

Implement insertionTabsEvenKeyCensus(drawers, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.

Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.
The input has exactly two rows, each containing at most 64 integers.

Target time O(q log(n+1)); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
